content.text:
I fixed the bug with a one-line change to the hard line break pattern in `src/rules.ts:286`. I haven't run anything: the folder has no `node_modules`, so neither the test suite nor your example has been run. **Cause:** the pattern that finds a hard break (`/^( {2,}|\\)\n(?!\s*$)/`) stopped right after the newline. Any spaces or tabs at the start of the next line were left behind as ordinary text, so they showed up after the `
`. **Fix:** the pattern now also consumes the spaces and tabs that follow the newline: ```ts const br = /^( {2,}|\\)\n[ \t]*(?!\s*$)/; ``` So `foo \n bar` and `foo\\\n\tbar` should both render as `

foo
bar

`. - **Other breaks:** the version used when the `breaks` option is on (every newline becomes `
`) is built from the same pattern, so it gets the fix too. - **Trailing breaks unchanged:** a break with only whitespace after it, e.g. at the end of a paragraph, still isn't treated as a hard break, as before. - **Existing tests:** the only unit test that checks a break token's raw text uses `a\nb` with nothing after the newline. That text stays `'\n'`, so the test should still pass.
